Compare models with leave-one-out cross-validation

Source: R/model_comparison.R
model_comparison.Rd

Compares fitted edge models by their expected predictive accuracy, estimated with Pareto-smoothed importance sampling leave-one-out cross-validation (PSIS-LOO) from the loo package, and returns model weights. Leave-one-out cross-validation measures how well a model predicts each observation when that observation is left out of the fit; PSIS-LOO approximates this without refitting the model. Use it to compare models with different terms, for example to test whether edge weights differ between dyads by comparing a model with a dyad() term against a null model with only an intercept.

Usage

model_comparison(models, ...)

Arguments

models

A list of two or more models fitted with bison_model(), ideally named. All models must be fitted to the same data (the same rows, in the same order).

...

Additional arguments passed to loo::loo_model_weights(), such as method = "pseudobma".

Value

The model weights returned by loo::loo_model_weights(), one per model, named after the elements of models. By default these are stacking weights.

Details

The model weights describe how much each model contributes to the best predictions: a model with a weight close to 1 predicts the data better than the others. loo may warn about high Pareto k values, which mean the approximation is unreliable for some observations; see loo::loo().

If the models have different numbers of posterior draws (for example because a chain failed), the same number of draws is taken at random from each model.

See also

bison_model()

Examples

# Test for non-random edge weights by comparing a model with edge weights
# against a null model where every dyad has the same rate of events.
sim_data <- simulate_bison_model("binary", aggregated = FALSE)
priors <- get_default_priors("binary")
fit_edge <- bison_model((event | effort) ~ dyad(node_1_id, node_2_id),
                        data = sim_data$df_sim, model_type = "binary", priors = priors)
#> Running MCMC with 4 parallel chains...
#> 
#> Chain 1 finished in 0.5 seconds.
#> Chain 2 finished in 0.5 seconds.
#> Chain 3 finished in 0.5 seconds.
#> Chain 4 finished in 0.5 seconds.
#> 
#> All 4 chains finished successfully.
#> Mean chain execution time: 0.5 seconds.
#> Total execution time: 0.8 seconds.
#> 
fit_null <- bison_model((event | effort) ~ 1,
                        data = sim_data$df_sim, model_type = "binary", priors = priors)
#> Running MCMC with 4 parallel chains...
#> 
#> Chain 1 finished in 0.3 seconds.
#> Chain 2 finished in 0.3 seconds.
#> Chain 3 finished in 0.3 seconds.
#> Chain 4 finished in 0.3 seconds.
#> 
#> All 4 chains finished successfully.
#> Mean chain execution time: 0.3 seconds.
#> Total execution time: 0.6 seconds.
#> 
model_comparison(list(non_random = fit_edge, random = fit_null))
#> Warning: Some Pareto k diagnostic values are too high. See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.
#> Method: stacking
#> ------
#>            weight
#> non_random 0.543 
#> random     0.457
